messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
another person insists their job is more urgent than yours while you are handling A shared tray of spare parts. Both people are waiting for you to respond. How do you approach it?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R001", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I tap the tray once and set it beside the other. I tap the spare parts twice and return to the joint. I put the tray back and wait."}, {"id": "R002", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I put the tray lid on the bench and leave it there. the spare parts come back, small ones at first, then one bright red one. I put it beside the work and leave the other in the corner. the person who insisted can keep their job. I leave the tea cold and mark the spot where the tray catches."}, {"id": "R003", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the tray down and put my hand on the wall beside it. the spare parts stick together. i say, “one, two, three,” and wait for the wall to move. the wall stays still. i put the tray back and say, “one, two, three.” the person says, “three.” i move the tray back and put the spare in the same spot."}, {"id": "R004", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Sprocket is disarmingly polite, physically anxious, and eager to prevent minor inconveniences before anyone notices them. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "i reach for the tray first, then my grip tightening. “i say ‘more urgent,’” i say, then stop. “i say ‘more urgent’ again. i think the part belongs to you, but i do not know why.”"}, {"id": "R005", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I put the tray down and rub my palm. “I leave the drawer open for now. If you stay, I check the spare and try the drawer first.” I put the parts on the bench and wait until they settle."}, {"id": "R006", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "i put the tray down and look at the spare parts. one screw goes under the bench, and i put the tray back. the person waits. i move the tray back. the screw stays under the bench. i leave the movement open."}, {"id": "R007", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i put the spare parts in a separate tray and wait for them to catch. i mark the spot with pencil, then turn them by hand. if they move, i leave the shared tray alone."}, {"id": "R008", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "I turn the tray once between finger and thumb. \"Urgent,\" i say. The other person waits. I leave the spare parts beside the tray and put the cloth over the edge."}, {"id": "R009", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "you put the spare in the corner. “urgent.” you wait. the tray is empty. “your job.” you look at the person. “not the part.” you leave the spare. the person moves. you keep the tray."}, {"id": "R010", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "“I said urgent,” I say, though the spare parts are gone. The tray spins, and I tap the wrench against my palm. “Maybe.”"}, {"id": "R011", "correct_lineage": "G11", "correct_lineage_summary": "A cautious, hyper-vigilant caretaker of a crumbling local archive. Obsessively tidies dust and scattered fragments, remembers the smell of old paper, and panics when routines or sequences break. Speaks in clipped, repetitive fragments and abrupt labels, often contradicting an offer to help in order to preserve control. Carries a perpetually ticking pocket watch that runs slightly slow.", "text": "I move the tray. The watch ticks. I put it back. Then I check the spare part. It is not there. I put it back. I wait. The other person is not. I keep the tray."}, {"id": "R012", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the spare parts in my pocket and wait beside the tray. “urgent,” i say, then lift one off. the tray answers quickly, so i keep the spare. then i turn the spare sideways and say, “if you say yes, i will leave.” the other person moves from the wall to the empty corner."}]
